title: The quotient onto a component ring is ind-etale
statement: For a ring $T$ and a connected component $Z$ of $\operatorname{Spec}T$, write $T_Z=T/I_Z$, where $I_Z$ is generated by the idempotents $e$ such that $Z\subseteq V(e)$; this is the component ring. For every commutative ring $T$ and every connected component $Z$ of $\operatorname{Spec}T$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], the quotient map $T\to T_Z$ is ind-etale [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. Consequently, if $T$ is an ind-etale $A$-algebra, then $T_Z$ is an ind-etale $A$-algebra; if all component rings of $T$ are henselian local [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], then $T_Z$ is also henselian local. Neither openness of $Z$ nor a finite number of components is assumed.

source.place: Tag 00EG (lemma-connected-component), component quotient by idempotents; Hübner–Schmidt §6 component convention, printed p. 12. Ind-etale composition is proetale.tex Tag 097K (lemma-composition-ind-etale).

proof.text: Let $E=\{e\in T:e^2=e,\ Z\subseteq V(e)\}$. Index by the small poset of finite subsets $F\subseteq E$, ordered by inclusion; it is nonempty (it contains $\varnothing$) and directed ($F\cup G$ dominates $F,G$). Put $J_F=(e:e\in F)$ and $d_F=1-\prod_{e\in F}(1-e)$. Products of commuting idempotents and their complements are idempotent, so $d_F^2=d_F$. The identity $d_{F\cup\{e\}}=d_F+e-d_Fe$ proves inductively that $d_F\in J_F$, and $ed_F=e$ for every $e\in F$ proves the reverse inclusion $J_F\subseteq(d_F)$. Thus $J_F=(d_F)$, including $J_\varnothing=(0)$. The quotient maps $B_F=T/J_F\to B_G=T/J_G$ for $F\subseteq G$ are well defined and form a diagram of $T$-algebras. These are explicit finite-product and ideal calculations.

source.place: Tag 00EH (lemma-ideal-is-squared-union-connected), explicit idempotent generator for a finite set of idempotents; elementary expansion

proof.text: For each $F$, the complementary element $u_F=1-d_F$ is idempotent. Apply part (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-fg-idempotent-ideal-idempotent-generator] to $R=T$, $e=u_F$ and the surjection $T\twoheadrightarrow B_F$, whose kernel is $J_F=(d_F)=(1-u_F)T$. It gives an isomorphism $T_{u_F}\cong B_F$ over $T$. In particular this identifies the structural map $T\to B_F$ with the principal localization map, rather than merely identifying their underlying rings.

By [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion], $\operatorname{Spec}T_{u_F}\to\operatorname{Spec}T$ is an open immersion. Part (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] makes it etale; the $T$-algebra isomorphism of Step 2 gives the same property for $\operatorname{Spec}B_F\to\operatorname{Spec}T$. Part (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-finite-presentation-localization] also gives finite presentation over $T$. Hence every stage of our diagram is an etale $T$-algebra of finite presentation.

source.place: Tag 00U2 (lemma-etale), part (1); scheme interpretation via schemes.tex Tag 01I3 and morphisms.tex Tag 02GP

proof.text: The maps $B_F\to T/I_Z$ form a cocone since $J_F\subseteq I_Z$. We verify the universal property in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] directly, so no colimit-existence hypothesis is needed. Given any compatible cocone $h_F:B_F\to C$ of $T$-algebras, let $g:T\to C$ be the composite $T\to B_\varnothing\xrightarrow{h_\varnothing}C$. For each $e\in E$, compatibility with $\varnothing\subseteq\{e\}$ implies $g(e)=0$, since $e$ vanishes in $B_{\{e\}}$. Thus $g$ kills the ideal $I_Z=(E)$ and defines a unique $T$-algebra map $\bar g:T/I_Z\to C$. For every $F$ and $t\in T$, compatibility gives $h_F(t\bmod J_F)=g(t)=\bar g(t\bmod I_Z)$, so this map factors every cocone leg. It is unique because $T\to T/I_Z$ is surjective. Consequently $T_Z=T/I_Z$ is the filtered colimit of the $B_F$ in $T$-algebras.

source.place: Tag 00EG (lemma-connected-component), component ideal generated by idempotents; explicit quotient universal-property argument

proof.text: Steps 1, 3 and 4 exhibit $T_Z$ as a small filtered colimit of etale $T$-algebras of finite presentation. This is exactly the definition of ind-etale in [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra], and proves that the specified quotient map $T\to T_Z$ is ind-etale. The construction uses finite subsets of the set $E$, not a finiteness assumption on the connected components.

source.place: Tag 097I (definition-ind-etale), applying the definition to the explicit presentation

proof.text: If $A\to T$ is ind-etale, the just-proved ind-etale map $T\to T_Z$ composes with it. Composition stability in [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability] therefore gives that the structural composite $A\to T\to T_Z$ is ind-etale.

Finally, if every component ring of $T$ is henselian local [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], apply that hypothesis to the chosen connected component $Z$: its component ring is $T_Z$ by the statement's definition. Thus $T_Z$ is henselian local. This is universal instantiation, with no transfer of henselianity across an arbitrary quotient. If $T$ is the zero ring, its spectrum has no connected component and the assertion quantified over $Z$ is vacuous.

source.place: Tag 00EG component convention; final clause is direct instantiation of the hypothesis

proof_origin.place: Explicit finite-idempotent presentation and quotient-colimit argument, using Tags 00EH (lemma-ideal-is-squared-union-connected), 00EG (lemma-connected-component) and 00U2 (lemma-etale), then proetale.tex 097K. This assembled deduction is written by Q11; no claim that 00EG itself states ind-etaleness.

lean.statement: theorem componentQuotient_indEtale (T : Type u) [CommRing T] (x : PrimeSpectrum T) : (Ideal.Quotient.mk (componentIdeal T x)).IndEtale ∧ (∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (f : A →+* T), f.IndEtale → ((Ideal.Quotient.mk (componentIdeal T x)).comp f).IndEtale) ∧ ((∀ y : PrimeSpectrum T, HenselianLocalRing (componentRing T y)) → HenselianLocalRing (componentRing T x))
lean.note: Uses the existing componentIdeal/componentRing from lem-trf-affine-etale-cover-component-criterion, added to stmt_deps solely to name the canonical construction. A point x indexes connectedComponent x; quantifying over all points covers exactly all nonempty connected components. RingHom.IndEtale fixes the canonical quotient map and, in the second conjunct, the composite A → T → T/I_Z.
